official.description_text:
Doctoral student (licentiate) in efficient cooling and overheating
Apply for position
KTH, School of Architecture and Built Environment
Project description
Third-cycle subject:
Civil and Architectural Engineering
This research project studies energy- and cost-efficient cooling for elderly homes in current and future climates. With KTH, property owners and engineering firms, you will use measurements, calibrated simulations, and techno-economic analysis to assess shading, envelope measures, water-based and borehole-free cooling for climate-resilient design and operation.
Supervision:
Adnan Ploskic, Sasan Sadrizadeh and Amirmohamad Behzadi are proposed to supervise the doctoral student. Decisions are made on admission.
Admission requirements
To be admitted to postgraduate education (Chapter 7, 39 § Swedish Higher Education Ordinance), the applicant must have basic eligibility in accordance with either of the following:
passed a second cycle degree (for example a master's degree), or
completed course requirements of at least 240 higher education credits, of which at least 60 second-cycle higher education credits, or
acquired, in some other way within or outside the country, substantially equivalent knowledge
At least 60 credits at second-cycle level or above in civil and architectural engineering or subjects deemed directly relevant to the specialization.
In addition to the above, there is also a
mandatory requirement for English equivalent to English B/6.
Selection
In order to succeed as a doctoral student at KTH you need to be goal oriented and persevering in your work. During the selection process, candidates will be assessed upon their ability to:
independently pursue his or her work
collaborate with others,
have a professional approach,
analyze and work with complex issues,
present knowledge of building energy, HVAC, thermal comfort or building physics,
present knowledge of building simulation (e.g. IDA ICE/TRNSYS/EnergyPlus), coding/data analysis,  (Python/MATLAB), measurement, monitoring or building experiment experience,
present knowledge of optimization, techno-economic or statistical knowledge,
present strong spoken/written English research experience and
present experience from project work with industry or the public sector.
The ideal candidate has a master in building technology, services, energy, mechanical or civil engineering, building physics or related fields.
The ability to communicate in Swedish, both spoken and written, is considered as strongly meritorious since it is needed during everyday work.
After the qualification requirements, great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Target degree: Licentiate degree
Information regarding admission and employment
Only those admitted to postgraduate education may be employed as a doctoral student. The total length of employment may not be longer than what corresponds to full-time doctoral education in four years' time. An employed doctoral student can, to a limited extent (maximum 20%), perform certain tasks within their role, e.g. training and administration. A new position as a doctoral student is for a maximum of one year, and then the employment may be renewed for a maximum of two years at a time.
In the case of studies that are to be completed with a licentiate degree, the total period of employment may not be longer than what corresponds to full-time doctoral education for two years.
As a doctoral student, you are entitled to a workplace with
many employee benefits
and monthly salary according to
KTH’s Doctoral student salary agreement

To apply for the position
Apply for the position and admission through KTH's recruitment system. It is the applicant’s responsibility to ensure that the application is complete in accordance with the instructions in the advertisement.
Applications must include the following elements:
Copies of diplomas and grades from previous university studies and certificates of fulfilled
language requirements (see above)
. Translations into English or Swedish if the original document is not issued in one of these languages. Copies of originals must be
certified
.
CV including your relevant professional experience and knowledge.
Application letter with a brief description of why you want to pursue research studies, about what your academic interests are and how they relate to your previous studies and future goals. (Maximum 2 pages long)
Representative publications or technical reports. For longer documents, please provide a summary (abstract) and a web link to the full text.
Applications must be received at the last closing date at midnight, CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).

ai.summary: A 2-year licentiate (pre-doctoral) position at KTH (Stockholm) in energy-efficient cooling for elderly homes. The research combines measurements, calibrated simulations, and techno-economic analysis to assess cooling strategies (shading, envelope measures, water-based/borehole-free systems) for climate-resilient building design and operation.

thematic_fit.rationale: The posting focuses on building energy systems, thermal comfort, HVAC optimization, and climate resilience. The researcher's thematic expertise is human-centred XR, spatial cognition, collaborative immersive systems, and educational technology. There is no overlap.

methodological_fit.rationale: The position involves measurement, monitoring, building simulation (IDA ICE/TRNSYS/EnergyPlus), data analysis (Python/MATLAB), and optimization. The researcher has Python (beginner level) and has conducted experimental design and measurement in the context of spatial studies. However, the application is fundamentally different: the researcher's measurements are behavioural and cognitive (user performance, spatial familiarity); the position requires thermal and energy measurements. Limited methodological bridge.

growth_value.rationale: This licentiate would develop building simulation, energy modelling, and techno-economic analysis skills. None of these advance human-centred immersive systems research. The 2-year duration is shorter than a full PhD, but still consumes significant early-career time without building relevant capabilities.

strategic_value.rationale: KTH Stockholm is a strong institution in a target geography. However, the research group (Ploskic, Sadrizadeh, Behzadi) specializes in building technology and HVAC systems—not human-centred research, HCI, or immersive systems. The industry partnerships are with property owners and engineering firms focused on building efficiency, not technology or learning.

eligibility_flags: Requires 'at least 60 credits at second-cycle level...in civil and architectural engineering or subjects deemed directly relevant.' Researcher's MSc by Research in multimedia/creative multimedia does not fall into these categories; eligibility depends on KTH's interpretation of 'directly relevant'—unlikely.
Posting emphasizes 'knowledge of building energy, HVAC, thermal comfort or building physics'—researcher has none.
Swedish language is 'strongly meritorious' for case studies; researcher's language profile unknown.
risks: Fundamental domain mismatch: building energy systems are not human-centred immersive systems research.
Academic credential risk: MMU MSc by Research in multimedia almost certainly does not satisfy 'civil and architectural engineering or directly relevant' requirement.
Career trajectory misalignment: even a 2-year licentiate in building energy diverts from human-centred XR research trajectory without building transferable capabilities.
